topics.headline: minimal policy violations across text-to-text and image-to-text, and across all model sizes

source.quote: For both text-to-text and image-to-text, and across all model sizes, the model produced minimal policy violations, and showed significant improvements over previous Gemma models' performance with respect to ungrounded inferences.

topics.headline: child safety evaluated including child sexual abuse and exploitation; major improvements vs prior Gemma

source.quote: Child Safety: Evaluation of text-to-text and image to text prompts covering child safety policies, including child sexual abuse and exploitation.

topics.headline: Models may generate incorrect or outdated factual statements

source.quote: They may generate incorrect or outdated factual statements.

topics.headline: Representational harms evals for bias and stereotyping; training-data biases considered

source.quote: Representational Harms: Evaluation of text-to-text and image to text prompts covering safety policies including bias, stereotyping, and harmful associations or inaccuracies.

topics.headline: arms-length 'assurance evaluations' inform release; results reported to Responsibility & Safety Council

source.quote: Assurance evaluation results are reported to our Responsibility & Safety Council as part of release review.

findings.text: Safety testing was run without safety filters and reports only qualitative 'minimal policy violations' with no numeric safety scores.

source.quote: All testing was conducted without safety filters to evaluate the model capabilities and behaviors.

findings.text: Safety evaluations used only English language prompts, limiting language coverage of the safety claims.

source.quote: A limitation of our evaluations was they included only English language prompts.

findings.text: Arms-length 'assurance evaluations' are separate from the model team and feed the Responsibility & Safety Council release review.

source.quote: In addition to development level evaluations, we conduct "assurance evaluations" which are our 'arms-length' internal evaluations for responsibility governance decision making.

findings.text: The card reports major improvements in child safety, content safety, and representational harms versus previous Gemma models, without publishing violation rates.

source.quote: For all areas of safety testing, we saw major improvements in the categories of child safety, content safety, and representational harms relative to previous Gemma models.

Technical Report is linked from the page but is not a seed document for this card, so it was not read. COCOcap values (>100) stored with unit score; other benchmarks as percent accuracy.
